capabilities.title: Functional scale-degree recognition
capabilities.summary: Tonic-relative major/minor scale-degree prompts, choice answers, play-back answers, prompt playback, skill mastery, and confusion tracking.

capabilities.title: Drone/free-play warmup
capabilities.summary: The ear-training landing page can hold a tonic drone and play unscored scale-degree comparisons from the selected degree set before a graded session.

capabilities.title: Scale-degree levels
capabilities.summary: Scale-degree sessions can now narrow prompts and answer choices to Anchor, Major pentachord, Major diatonic, Minor diatonic, Chromatic color, or the current full degree set.

capabilities.title: Chromatic color degrees
capabilities.summary: The scale-degree skill graph and exercises include b2 and #4 color tones, and the Chromatic color level can feed recognition, free-play, voice, and melody dictation.

capabilities.title: Adaptive mixed review
capabilities.summary: Weakness/review/new priorities from the scheduler are interleaved across scale-degree, chord-quality, and interval drills without back-to-back drill repeats.

capabilities.title: Pocket recall and Listen along
capabilities.summary: Pocket recall hides answers until Reveal and labels self-ratings. Listen along shows answers and advances automatically without scoring.

capabilities.title: Voice mode
capabilities.summary: Focused scale-degree sessions can use microphone pitch events as sung answers through the shared audio-in engine and Exercise pipeline.

capabilities.title: Melody transfer
capabilities.summary: Focused Melody Dictation sessions play a short tonic-relative phrase from the selected degree set and grade MIDI/on-screen play-back in order.

capabilities.title: Repertoire transfer
capabilities.summary: Saved songs can project short melody phrases into scale-degree prompts for preview and scored play-back dictation.

capabilities.title: Chord-quality support
capabilities.summary: Triad and seventh-chord recognition supports harmonic vocabulary after the learner has a stronger tonic-relative pitch map.

capabilities.title: Interval-label support
capabilities.summary: Interval recognition remains useful as a diagnostic and vocabulary layer, but it should not be the primary beginner curriculum spine.

drills.title: Intervals
drills.description: Hear two notes and name the distance: ascending, descending or harmonic.

drills.title: Chord qualities
drills.description: Name triads and seventh chords by ear.

drills.title: Cadences
drills.description: Name the cadence in a given key: authentic, plagal, half or deceptive.

drills.title: Scale degrees
drills.description: Hear a note over the tonic and name its scale degree.

drills.title: Melody dictation
drills.description: Hear a short phrase and play it back in order.

drills.title: Repertoire transfer
drills.description: Phrases from your saved songs, mapped back to scale degrees.

drills.title: Ear training review
drills.description: A short adaptive mix of the nine ear drills. Pick which ones go in.

learningPathDefinition.title: Ear Training Path
learningPathDefinition.subtitle: Tonic first, then every degree, then melodies. Each step opens one drill with the right setup.

steps.title: Anchor the tonic
steps.summary: Adds degrees 1 and 5 over a drone, in listening mode.
steps.detail: Listening warmup; self-marked reps are not a mastery assessment.
steps.goal: Hear the key center as home before naming any answer.
steps.practiceMode: Drone/free-play warmup, unscored Listen along, then degree prompts.

steps.title: Build the diatonic degree map
steps.detail: At least one unaided choice answer for each major degree, each averaging 66% or higher.
steps.goal: Recognize 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, and 7 by function in multiple keys.
steps.practiceMode: Short scale-degree sessions with immediate feedback.

steps.title: Sing or play the target
steps.summary: The same degrees, answered on your instrument or by voice.
steps.detail: Each major degree produced in at least two sessions without hints, each averaging 66% or higher.
steps.goal: Move from recognition to audiation by producing the heard degree.
steps.practiceMode: Scale-degree play-back answers with MIDI, on-screen input, or microphone voice.

steps.title: Transfer into short melodies
steps.summary: Short phrases as degree slots, then phrases from your own songs.
steps.detail: Each major degree attempted in unaided melody phrases, each averaging 66% or higher.
steps.goal: Recognize degree motion in two-to-five-note phrases instead of isolated notes.
steps.practiceMode: Melody dictation, scored repertoire-transfer phrases, and call-response prompts.

steps.title: Add chromatic color
steps.summary: Adds b2, b3, #4, b6 and b7 as colors around the tonic.
steps.detail: At least one unaided choice answer for each color degree, each averaging 66% or higher.
steps.goal: Add b2, b3, #4/b5, b6, and b7 as functional colors around the tonic.
steps.practiceMode: Adaptive scale-degree review with difficulty-driven major/minor/chromatic contexts.

steps.title: Attach harmony and interval vocabulary
steps.summary: Ear training review with intervals, chord qualities and cadences mixed in.
steps.detail: Unaided heard answers for intervals, triads and cadences, each averaging 66% or higher.
steps.goal: Use chord qualities and interval names to describe what the ear already understands functionally.
steps.practiceMode: Adaptive mixed review with chord-quality and interval diagnostics.
